original.target_description: Original article identity verified; assigned Study 7 and target test unresolved. Candidate experiments and tests retained in notes.

notes: Identity assessed independently: supplied canonical text is a PMC web parse of the primary research article Hiding personal information reveals the worst, Leslie K John, Kate Barasz, Michael I Norton; Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 113(4):954–959; DOI 10.1073/pnas.1516868113, matching ref_o. It contains the main report, methods and references, and names but does not include pnas.1516868113.sapp.pdf. No PDF was supplied. The supplementary file was not accessed. Target cannot be uniquely identified: supplied study_o is 7, whereas the source uses Experiment 1, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, 4A and 4B. There is no explicit correspondence to Study 7, and supplied p.17/p.10 locators are not identifiable within this unpaginated main-article parse. Mapping 7 to 4B by sequence would violate the instruction against assigning targets by order. The neutral description spans the entire paper and does not isolate a condition, outcome or test. Candidate evidence only, not extracted target values: Experiment 4B prints participant N = 608, without final group counts or explicit contrast-specific analytic Ns; omnibus chi-square(2) = 11.41, P = 0.003; No Drugs versus Baseline chi-square(1) = 2.26, P = 0.14; Trustworthy versus No Drugs chi-square(1) = 11.31, P = 0.001; Trustworthy versus Baseline chi-square(1) = 3.49, P = 0.07. No d is supplied in that main-text results paragraph. These distinct tests cannot be interchanged. Another substantive candidate is Experiment 4A, which prints N = 206 for combined employee/employer roles, employee withholding z = 4.20, P < 0.0001, and employer hiring t(99) = 2.12, P = 0.04; the methods also give frequency-condition chi-square(1) = 2.44, P = 0.12. Combined-role N is not assumed analytic N for any such contrast. Earlier experiments also address the broad description. No numeric target was selected, N derived, metric converted, or source-wide absence inferred. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders only; no replication source was inspected.
